blockers.claim: §4 DDL section names the new table file `src/database/tables/03-user-sessions.sql` (hedged only with "verify 03 is free; else next free NN"), and SP1's packet instructions say to embed §4 verbatim.
blockers.evidence: Live tree: `yhealth-app/server/src/database/tables/03-consent-records.sql` already exists (confirmed via `ls`), and is registered in `setup.ts` TABLE_FILES right after `02-users.sql`. `03` is not free — the actual next-free 2-digit prefix is >145 (highest existing numeric prefix in `tables/` is `145-resource-recommendations.sql`, with a pre-existing `139-*` duplicate already on record in memory as a known gap). The plan's own worked example in §4 uses `03-user-sessions.sql` as the literal filename, which is what gets embedded into the SP1 packet per §7 ("embed §4 DDL verbatim").
blockers.fix: Pick an actual free number (e.g. next after 145, or 146+) before packet composition, verify with `ls src/database/tables/ | sort -n`, and correct the DDL section and SP1 packet target filename before any worker touches it. A GLM worker following the packet literally risks colliding with or overwriting `03-consent-records.sql`.

blockers.claim: SP1's acceptance criterion states `npm run db:migrate:auto` will apply the new `user_sessions` table to an existing DB idempotently, purely because a new timestamped file is dropped in `src/database/migrations/` — the plan explicitly says this file is "discovered/run by scripts/migrate.ts" and "does not need adding to the hardcoded run-migrations.ts array."
blockers.evidence: `db:migrate:auto` → `src/scripts/migrate.ts` → `autoMigrate()` in `src/database/auto-migrate.ts`. Read in full: `autoMigrate()` computes `missingTables = EXPECTED_TABLES.filter(t => !existingTables.includes(t))` against a hardcoded `EXPECTED_TABLES` array (lines 11-369) of table *names* — `user_sessions` is not in that array. Only tables present in `EXPECTED_TABLES` (and, for the individual-migration branch, in the `migrationTableMap` keyed by table name at lines ~1394-1427) trigger any file lookup in `migrations/`. Files in `migrations/` are otherwise only run if hardcoded into the `SUPPLEMENTARY_MIGRATIONS` array (lines 1112-1291), which is exactly the mechanism the codebase's own convention uses for a comparable recent table add (`'20260707120000_contract_witnesses.sql'` — comment: "mirrors tables/140-contract-witnesses.sql"). A bare new timestamped file that is in neither list is never read by `autoMigrate()`. This is also precisely the class of bug documented in R2/memory as the `139-life-area-checkins.sql` gap — but the plan's fix for that gap (`\dt` verification + psql fallback) treats it as an execution-time check, not a design defect in the packet itself, so the same failure mode is reintroduced by SP1 as written.
blockers.fix: Either (a) add `'user_sessions'` to `EXPECTED_TABLES` in `auto-migrate.ts` and register the table name → migration file in `migrationTableMap`, or (b) — matching the codebase's actual convention for this exact scenario — add the new migration filename to `SUPPLEMENTARY_MIGRATIONS` (unconditional, idempotent, re-run every deploy). Update SP1's packet and acceptance criteria accordingly; the plan's evidence table (row 36, citing scope-db-schema §4) inherited scope-db-schema.md's inaccurate description of `scripts/migrate.ts` as generically discovering timestamped files, which the live `auto-migrate.ts` code does not do.

blockers.claim: ADR-7 claims Apple sign-in "works in Expo Go on iOS because the Expo Go app itself declares the Sign in with Apple entitlement," and frames Apple as "the primary Expo-Go-verifiable social path" (also load-bearing for R4's mitigation of the Google Expo-Go gap). ADR-5 then configures server-side JWKS verification to accept only `APPLE_CLIENT_IDS` = the app's own native bundle id `ai.xyric.balencia` (plus an optional web Service ID) as the token audience.
blockers.evidence: These two ADRs contradict each other internally. If, as ADR-7 states, the Sign-in-with-Apple entitlement actually used at runtime under Expo Go belongs to the Expo Go app itself (not the target app), the identity token Apple issues will carry Expo Go's own app identifier as its `aud` claim — not `ai.xyric.balencia`. `jose.jwtVerify(idToken, jwks, { audience: APPLE_CLIENT_IDS })` (ADR-5) will then reject every Expo-Go-originated Apple sign-in with a wrong-`aud` 401, precisely the "reject bad sig / wrong aud / expired" behavior SP2's own acceptance criteria demand. The plan never states what audience value an Expo-Go Apple token actually carries, never adds Expo Go's own identifier to `APPLE_CLIENT_IDS`, and neither R3 (which only discusses Simulator identity-token *depth*, a different concern) nor R4 (which only discusses Google's redirect/client-id problem) covers this audience-mismatch failure mode at all.
blockers.fix: Resolve the contradiction before building SP2/MP3/MP7: either (a) verify empirically (real device/Simulator running the Expo Go client, not a dev build) what `aud` an `expo-apple-authentication` identity token actually carries under Expo Go, and if it differs from the app's bundle id, add that value to the accepted-audiences set with a documented justification, or (b) if Expo Go genuinely cannot produce a token verifiable against the app's own identity, retract the "Apple is the primary Expo-Go-verifiable path" claim, mark Apple gated-in-Expo-Go like Google, and update R4/SMK's scope accordingly — otherwise the batch's stated Expo-Go-Simulator social-auth deliverable is unverifiable as designed.

majors.claim: ADR-3's "Why" argues legacy web refresh tokens "migrate silently within their 7-day window" via the dual-read `/refresh` lazy-migration path, and the plan's backward-compat evidence (row 37, citing scope-web-client §7) treats `/refresh`'s dual-read as the operative web-compatibility surface.
majors.evidence: Traced the actual web client: `yhealth-app/client/lib/auth.ts` `jwt` callback only captures `token.backendAccessToken`/`token.backendRefreshToken` inside `if (user)` (lines 203-216), i.e. only at initial sign-in — there is no code path anywhere that updates these fields after the fact. `yhealth-app/client/app/api/auth/backend-session/route.ts` reads those same static, login-time-captured values out of the encrypted NextAuth JWT and re-writes them as the HttpOnly `access_token`/`refresh_token` cookies on every reinstall call. `yhealth-app/client/lib/api-client.ts` lines 156-204 show the web client's *entire* 401-recovery strategy is `reinstallBackendSession()` (lines 500-529) — a `fetch('/api/auth/backend-session', ...)` call — followed by logout if the retried request still 401s. A repo-wide grep for `/auth/refresh` in `yhealth-app/client` (excluding the backend-session cookie-path string literal) returns zero call sites; there is no Next.js proxy route at `/api/auth/refresh`, and no `middleware.ts` exists. In other words, the web client appears to never directly call the Express `POST /auth/refresh` endpoint that ADR-3's dual-read modifies. The plan cites scope-web-client §7 as its evidence for "401→reinstall-or-logout" but does not draw the consequence: `/refresh`'s lazy-migration branch may rarely-to-never actually execute for pure-web users, so the "legacy tokens migrate within 7 days" and future "safe to drop `users.refresh_token`" claims (ADR-3) are unverified for that population, and SP10's "web-compat regression" test (asserting the no-sid `/refresh` response is byte-identical) does not exercise the actual live web recovery path at all.
majors.fix: Either confirm (with a live trace/log capture against the running system) that `/auth/refresh` genuinely is invoked for web sessions through some path not found in this review, or explicitly acknowledge in the plan that web-session backward compatibility is governed by the `reinstallBackendSession`/NextAuth-JWT-cache mechanism (unaffected either way by this batch, since it never rotates), and drop or reframe the "legacy tokens migrate silently" claim to apply to mobile only. This does not change BIOS-003's behavior for web (nothing gets worse), but the plan's stated migration-completeness rationale needs correcting, and the future column-drop batch needs to account for potentially-permanent unmigrated web-only legacy rows.

majors.claim: ADR-1/SP3's `rotateSession(sessionId, presentedToken, newRefreshToken): Promise<'rotated'|'reuse_detected'|'not_found'>` contract does not specify atomic (compare-and-swap) SQL semantics, and R5's mitigation for "reuse detection false-positive locks out a legit client mid-rotation" relies on client-side single-flight guards rather than server-side atomicity.
majors.evidence: A naive implementation (SELECT current hash → compare in application code → UPDATE) is subject to a TOCTOU race: two genuinely-concurrent refresh requests presenting the same still-valid current token (e.g. a background task and a foreground app-resume racing, or a retried request that the mobile client's single-flight guard didn't catch because it originated from a second process/widget) would both read the same matching hash, both proceed past the compare, and both issue a UPDATE — producing two divergent valid-looking token pairs for one session row, only one of which the row now reflects. R5 states the risk is mitigated by mobile's existing single-flight refresh plus "test the concurrent case," but neither SP9's unit-test case list nor SP10's integration-test case list (§7, §8) actually enumerates a concurrent/simultaneous-refresh-on-the-same-session test.
majors.fix: Specify `rotateSession` as a single atomic SQL statement, e.g. `UPDATE user_sessions SET refresh_token_hash = $new, last_used_at = now() WHERE id = $sid AND refresh_token_hash = $old_hash AND revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING id`, treating a zero-row result as either `reuse_detected` (row exists but hash didn't match) or `not_found`/`revoked` (disambiguate with a follow-up SELECT only for error messaging, not for the security decision). Add an explicit concurrent-refresh-race test case to SP9 or SP10's embedded fixture list so a packet-literal worker actually builds it.

majors.claim: SP7 says: "Targets: modify `logout` in `auth-session.controller.ts`; add `allDevices?:boolean` to logout validator (`src/validators/auth.validator.ts`)" — implying an existing logout validator schema is being extended.
majors.evidence: scope-server-auth.md's route trace shows `POST /logout | authenticate | none | logout` — no `validate(...)` middleware is currently registered on the logout route at all (unlike every other body-bearing route, which lists a Zod schema). There is nothing to "add `allDevices?` to" — a new schema and its wiring into `auth.routes.ts`'s middleware chain must be created from scratch.
majors.fix: Correct SP7 to say "create a new optional `logoutSchema` (`{ allDevices: z.boolean().optional() }`) and wire `validate(logoutSchema)` into the `/logout` route's middleware chain," not "add to" an existing validator.

minors.claim: SP9's embedded test guidance ("mock `jwtVerify` to throw the specific error classes") doesn't enumerate which `jose` error classes (e.g. `JWTExpired`, `JWTClaimValidationFailed`, `JWSSignatureVerificationFailed`) map to which of the five listed Apple-verifier failure modes.
minors.evidence: §7 SP9 acceptance list: "Apple verifier failure modes (bad signature, wrong `aud`, expired `exp`, missing `sub`, missing `email`) each → `null`" — but `jose`'s exported error taxonomy differs materially from `jsonwebtoken`'s (which the rest of the codebase's existing auth tests are patterned on, per scope-server-auth §6), and the packet doesn't name which `jose` export to import/throw in the mock.
minors.fix: Embed the exact `jose` error class names (from the `jose` package's `errors` export) in the SP9 packet when it's composed, so the GLM worker doesn't have to guess or hallucinate the API.

minors.claim: SP8's target line-range for the Apple/Google fall-through it replaces ("the exact fall-through lines being replaced (337-361)") doesn't precisely match the two different citations in the plan's own evidence table vs. scope-server-auth.md.
minors.evidence: Architecture plan §2 row 5 cites `auth-registration.controller.ts:337` for the Google-only verify call and `:357-361` for the Apple fall-through; SP8 in §7 collapses this to a single `337-361` range. Not a functional defect, but imprecise enough that a packet composer copying it verbatim could target the wrong span.
minors.fix: When composing the SP8 packet, re-derive the exact current line numbers from source rather than reusing the plan's rounded range.

verified_ok: ADR-3's dual-read requires no changes to `verifyRefreshToken` itself: the middleware already passes the full decoded JWT payload through as `req.user` (`auth.middleware.ts` `verifyRefreshToken`), so `decoded.sessionId` being `undefined` for legacy (no-sid) tokens naturally falls through to the unchanged legacy branch with zero risk of breaking the JWT-verification step for existing tokens.

ADR-4's this-device-logout design is consistent with ADR-2: since `generateTokens` signs `sessionId` into *both* access and refresh tokens when provided, the `logout` handler (which runs under `authenticate`/access-token, not `verifyRefreshToken`) will have `req.user.sessionId` available post-migration, so ADR-4's sid-present/absent branching is implementable without further signature changes.

S05b's link-token-to-OTP deviation (ADR-9) is honestly framed and explicitly flagged as a documented adaptation, matching canon's honesty invariant and the actual `/reset-password` contract traced in scope-server-auth §4.

The consent screen (S03c → `POST /consent`) and the WhatsApp skip path (S03e → `POST /whatsapp/skip`, primary action) are both present in the mobile flow map (§6) and packet decomposition (MP5/MP8) — neither slice is silently dropped.

Reuse-detection-revokes-the-whole-session is a strict security improvement over the current single-slot mismatch-only 401 (which does not revoke anything beyond the one comparison) — this is additive, not a downgrade of the existing 'replay of an old refresh token → 401' guarantee.
SP8's 'account-linking-by-email preserved' correctly matches the existing `socialAuth()` linking-by-email behavior traced in scope-server-auth §3, which the plan does not otherwise alter.

The five-slice scope (server session model, mobile refresh alignment, Apple/Google verification, registration/OTP/forgot-reset, token security review) is consistently reflected in the Wave 0-7 packet decomposition with no unrelated screens or endpoints introduced.
